description_preview:
Who We Are
Headquartered in Nashville, Tennessee, Ncontracts leads the industry in integrated risk management and compliance solutions, serving over 5,000 financial institutions nationwide. As a seven-time Inc. 5000 Fastest Growing Companies honoree and consistent year-over-year recipient of "Best Places to Work" awards, we offer a thriving, work environment where career growth and life-work balance go hand in hand.
At Ncontracts, you'll join a team of industry experts dedicated to strengthening the financial services sector through innovation and thought leadership. We're seeking creative, collaborative, and self-driven professionals across all areas of our business - from developing cutting-edge solutions to sales, marketing, customer support, and beyond. Join us in our mission to make the financial industry stronger and more resilient, while advancing your career in a supportive, dynamic environment that values your unique skills and perspectives.
About The Role
We’re currently looking for a few Senior Developers to join the team and help us build and integrate our products. At this level you own the architecture and delivery of large features within a squad – applying deep, in-depth expertise to complex problems, making the technology and architecture decisions for your team, and frequently advising and mentoring others. You exercise strong independent judgment and are accountable for outcomes that matter to your team and the products you build.
As an engineering organization we’ve come to share several common beliefs:
We believe that it’s possible to build applications in a sustainable and repeatable way.
We believe that user story mapping, design sprints, and close collaboration with product folks are the best way to determine what needs to be worked on.
We believe that Kanban keeps our development efforts flowing forward and helps proactively identify bottlenecks.
We believe finishing is better than starting.
We believe that small teams working on well-defined projects for a set amount of time ensures that we build the most valuable things first and allows for a predictable date of completion.
We don’t believe in estimating individual stories. Ever.
A Senior Developer at Ncontracts is expected to exhibit the following behaviors:
Leadership by example: Use best practices for development, communicate excellently both inside and outside the organization, manage interpersonal relationships well, and lead by example in code reviews and technical discussions.
Architecture ownership: You architect large features and services, make the technology and architecture decisions for your team, and lead architectural reviews and decision-making – balancing technical excellence with pragmatic delivery.
Intentional mentorship: Ncontracts is dedicated to teaching and growing talent, and at this level mentorship is expected. You mentor other developers formally and informally and help create learning opportunities for the team.
AI-forward engineering: You integrate AI agents or assistants into your workflow to move faster while critically evaluating their output – catching subtle bugs and security issues in AI-generated code and helping establish sensible AI usage guidelines for your team.
Instinctive troubleshooting: Rapid diagnosis and resolution of bugs and problems is essential to a productive team. You debug complex issues across the stack quickly and are frequently consulted by others for difficult problems.
Honesty: Whether reviewing another developer’s code, participating in retrospectives, or working with your team on what direction to take a project, we expect openness and honesty. Honesty creates trust, and we believe that all great teams are built on trust.
Low ego: Have confidence in your skills and experience, but be willing to alter your opinions and ideas when another, better one comes along. Have strong opinions, but loosely held.
Deep curiosity: You’ll be expected to research new and exciting technologies, perfect the use of existing technologies, and discover new libraries and tools that can affect change across the organization.
Motivation: You’re a natural self-starter, and you enjoy solving problems. You are capable of jumping in with minimal instruction and figuring out what should be done.
It’s Expected You’ll Have The Following
Expertise in one or more of the following languages and their common frameworks: C#, JavaScript/TypeScript, Python
Experience building services and APIs in cloud platforms like Azure or AWS
Understanding of API security and OAuth
Strong knowledge of SQL and relational databases
Experience designing and architecting large features or services
Experience embedding AI and LLM capabilities into products
Experience writing unit and integration tests
Knowledge of instrumentation and observability techniques
Experience building and working with CI/CD pipelines
Experience mentoring other developers
Experience giving and receiving code reviews, both live and written
Typical experience for this level: a Bachelor’s degree plus ~8 years, a Master’s plus ~6 years, a PhD plus ~3 years, or equivalent depth of demonstrated impact.
It’s helpful for you to have at least some of the following:
Experience working in horizontally scaling systems
Experience in or familiarity with message/event-driven architecture patterns and distributed systems architecture
Familiarity with agentic development workflows and AI coding assistants (e.g., Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Devin)
Familiarity with systems integration
Experience working with an integrated design team
An automation mindset
We Offer All Full-time Team Members
A fun, fast-paced work environment
Responsible PTO Plan that meets or exceeds state and local medical and family leave laws
11 paid holidays
Community and social events to keep you connected and engaged
Mental Health Benefits
Medical, Dental and Vision insurance
Company-paid Group Life Insurance, Short- and Long-Term Disability

We’re looking for a Level 5 Senior Developer to set technical direction beyond a single team. Where our Level 4 Senior Developers own the architecture and delivery of large features within a squad, a Level 5 Senior Developer operates across squads: defining the standards, patterns, and platform capabilities that multiple teams build on. You’ll work on significant and unique problems, exercise independent judgment, and be accountable for technical outcomes that impact the whole R&D function.

Force multiplier: You mentor Senior (L4) developers and help them reach the next level, develop future technical leaders, and create reusable knowledge – documentation, patterns, and tooling – that raises the bar across teams.
Strategic ownership: You identify and drive organization-wide improvements, take ownership of strategic technical initiatives, and see them through obstacles. You apply economic thinking and pragmatic tradeoffs to decisions that affect the whole function.
AI-forward engineering: You define how teams use AI assistants and AI-powered capabilities effectively – establishing practices, evaluating and piloting emerging tooling, and ensuring acceleration never comes at the cost of quality or security.

Low ego: Have confidence in your skills and experience, but be willing to alter your opinions when a better idea comes along. Strong opinions, loosely held – and the maturity to build consensus rather than win arguments.
Deep curiosity: You research emerging technologies, evaluate them rigorously, and drive adoption of the ones that move the organization forward.

Deep, demonstrated expertise in one or more of the following languages and their ecosystems: C#, JavaScript/TypeScript, Python

Strong API design and security experience at scale, including OAuth

Experience integrating AI/LLM capabilities into production systems
A track record of mentoring senior engineers and leading technical strategy across more than one team
Experience giving and receiving code reviews, both live and written

Experience with vector databases, RAG, and agentic AI patterns
Multi-region, high-availability, or disaster-recovery architecture experience
Experience harmonizing UI/design systems across multiple products
Familiarity with systems integration and working with an integrated design team

An automation mindset

description_preview:
Company Description
LeadX is the maker of Lex, an AI sales assistant designed to help tech-savvy agency owners generate high-quality leads more efficiently. Lex enables users to scout leads with filters tailored to agencies and hyper-personalize outreach using built demos. LeadX focuses on leveraging AI to streamline sales workflows and improve conversion rates. The team is dedicated to building intuitive, data-driven tools that empower agencies to grow their business through smarter lead generation. Joining LeadX means contributing to a product that sits at the intersection of AI, sales, and agency growth.
The role
You'll be one of the first engineers here, and you'll own real product, not a corner of it. This is a zero-to-one seat: AI agents that find leads, generate real websites, and run outreach, plus everything holding them up. You'll ship to production every week, talk to the people using it, and make the calls that decide where the product goes next.
What success looks like a year from now
- The core agent loop (find, build, pitch) is faster, sharper, and more reliable than it is today, and you own the systems that got it there.
- Features you shipped are the reason people tell someone else about LeadX.
- When something breaks at 2am, you're the one who understands why, fixes it, and makes sure it can't happen twice.
- The whole team moves faster because you're here.
What you'll own
- The AI agents end to end: the prompts and models, the pipelines behind them, and the product people actually touch.
- Whole features, solo, from the idea to the deploy to watching how users react.
- A live production system (real users, real payments, real data) kept healthy as it grows.
- What we build next, as much as how we build it.
You'll thrive here if
- You ship. You'd rather put something live and learn than plan it to death.
- You build across the whole stack and don't need the exact framework handed to you. We work with modern web, Python, and LLMs/agents, but we care that you can learn and ship anything, not that you've used our specific tools.
- You actually want to build with AI agents, not just ride the wave.
- You want ownership, not tickets. Ambiguity makes you move, not freeze.
- You care about the user and the business, not only the code.
This is not for you if you want a narrow, well-defined lane, a big team to lean on, or scope that never surprises you. Founding engineering is fast, wide, and sometimes messy. That's the job.
How to apply
Send [your email / link] a short note: something you've built that you're proud of,
and one thing you'd change about LeadX after five minutes of using it.
Skip the formal cover letter.

title: Forward Deployed Engineer - US intern
reason: Stack +14; Title fit +6; Entry +15; US +10
description_preview:
Junior / early career. San Francisco.
"Hire people who make you never want to hire 'normal' people again." — Brian Chesky
Every sales team has the same problem: find the right companies, qualify them, get there before anyone else. But no two teams solve it the same way - a rep at L'Oréal qualifies a lead nothing like a rep at Deel. Same problem, completely different workflow. Generic tools hand everyone the same generic workflow, which is exactly why every team using them plateaus in the same place.
Leadbay qualifies leads for agentic workflows. Teams at L'Oréal, Saint-Gobain, Gerflor USA, Corgi, and Nespresso B2B have 3x'd their addressable market and 10x'd what they defined as a qualified lead.
Those numbers are real because someone sat with each of those teams and built their specific workflow. Not a template. Theirs.
Right now that someone is a founder. That is the bottleneck, and it is the entire reason this job exists.
We raised $4.3M to become the first billion-dollar MCP-native company (Model Context Protocol) - and you'll build daily alongside the founders, Ludo (previous US investor in Startup who’ve worked with hundreds of CEOs) and Milan (PhD in making AI work with limited data, exited Sepage to Travelsoft).
Founders' view on the role
One loop, four steps: Land → Listen → Ship → Expand.
You land the account after signature. Signature is not success. Success is the day their reps open Leadbay before their CRM.
You listen to what actually happens inside the account. Not what the customer requests on a call. What they do, where they hesitate, which lead they skipped and why.
You ship. Specific skills, widgets, artifacts, lenses, qualification prompts, imports, connectors, prospecting agents - all powered by Leadbay AI. Power users start using them; some work, some don't; and suddenly you hit a 10x that couldn't be done before. That's when you help expand, and it compounds at company scale.
Along the way, you build your own knowledge that helps the next account go 5 to 10x too. Some of it lives in one account forever. The best of it graduates into the product.
Whatever the account size, you're always in front of the person who owns growth: a CEO, a C-level, a Head of. And no two weeks look alike.
What You'll Do
Land small accounts in 30-minute calls, and show them how to build what couldn't be done before.
Land large accounts over days in their offices, understand their growth strategy, and build the workflow with them.
Build everything that needs building inside our MCP product and MCP acquisition funnel.
Use your own MCP to become a living example of the most efficient sales rep in the world.
Here's what your first 30 / 60 / 90 days look like: 30 days meeting as many self-serve users as you can and shipping as many agentic systems as possible; 60 days building your library of what works; 90 days building your own skillset and walking into the offices of much bigger customers.
Who You Are
Technically capable and socially skilled. Both. Not one.
You can be in a room with a VP of Sales at 9am and writing Python at 2pm, and you're not faking either one.
You probably have nothing on your CV that predicts success here. No FDE title, maybe not the right degree, maybe not much work experience at all. We care about what you've built and how you think.
You spend evenings building AI skills, vibe-coding side projects, testing new tools, figuring things out because you enjoy it. You're usually the first person you know to try the new thing.
You'd rather ship something hacky that works today than something clean next month. You're comfortable saying "I don't know, let me go find out" in front of a customer.
Leadbay is part of a much bigger career journey (most likely toward becoming a YC founder). Ludo, Milan, and the broader YC ecosystem will help you grow fast.
We're not a great fit for people who need to be told exactly what to do, struggle to make judgment calls, wait for constant validation, or care more about "whose fault is it?" than "how do we make it work?"
We work low-overhead. One weekly team coordination meeting, everything else in service of doing the work. GitHub Projects, weekly iterations, English.

Data.

You’d own ETL pipelines carrying operational data from the ERP, storefronts and logistics into it — building them, instrumenting them, and fixing them when a schema changes upstream on a Friday afternoon. Real data engineering inside a full-stack role.
Integrations.
This is event-driven, not a request-response monolith. Webhooks and events move state between the ERP, tenant systems and logistics providers. You’d design those contracts: idempotency, retries, ordering, and what happens when a downstream system drops for six hours and comes back wanting everything at once. Get this layer wrong and the warehouse feels it.
APIs.
REST, designed properly. Versioning and rate limiting as decisions made up front, not patches applied after an integration partner takes production down.
Front end.
Custom headless storefronts against a modern headless CMS — Sanity, Contentful, Strapi and that class of tooling. Custom means custom. This isn’t theming a template.
Delivery.
GitHub Actions, automated deployments, CI/CD as standard. Testing discipline came up unprompted — UAT and integration testing specifically, because when an ERP writes to a warehouse, an untested integration has physical consequences.
Essential Skills
•   2–5 years building full-stack web applications, genuinely across the stack
•   REST API design with real opinions on versioning and rate limiting
•   Cloud platform experience — operating in it, not just deploying to it
•   Git, GitHub Actions or equivalent, owning your own CI/CD
•   Evidence you test things properly
•   AI tooling as a working habit, with the judgement to know which output to trust and which to bin
Strongly wanted:
ETL and pipeline work, BigQuery, headless CMS, event-driven systems, or any exposure to ERP, warehousing or logistics.

title: Software Engineer - Network HW Enablement & Cloud Infrastructure
reason: Stack +40; Synergy +8; Title fit +12; US +10; Senior salary -45
description_preview:
One of our Software Groups at Red Hat has an opening for a Software Engineer with experience in Linux, Kubernetes and Networking. In this role, you’ll be joining the team that makes sure Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) and OpenShift play nice with the latest networking hardware (SmartNICs and DPUs). Think of yourself as the bridge between the physical hardware and the cloud software. You aren't just building apps; you’re making sure the foundation they sit on is rock solid.
What Your Day-to-Day Looks Like
Write & Implement Code: You’ll spend most of your time in the "flow state," writing C, Python, or Go to integrate new hardware features into our core platforms.
Troubleshoot & Debug: When hardware doesn't talk to the OS correctly, you’ll dig into the drivers and the Linux kernel to find out why and fix it.
Smart Automation: You’ll identify repetitive manual tasks (like testing or deployment) and write scripts to automate them so the whole team stays fast.
Collaborate & Ship: You’ll work alongside senior engineers to take requirements and turn them into functional, enterprise-grade code that actually works for customers.
Innovate with AI: Act as a technical explorer, proactively researching and integrating emerging AI technologies into our software development lifecycle to optimize workflows, tooling, and efficiency.
What You Will Bring to the Table
Solid Linux Skills: You know your way around a Linux terminal and have a good grasp of how the kernel handles networking and drivers. You don't need to be a kernel deity, but you should know how things connect.
Some experience with Networking
Polyglot Coding: You are comfortable writing C (for the low-level stuff) and either Python or Go (for tooling and automation). You’re less worried about "which language" and more worried about "does it work?"
A "Testing" Mindset: You write code that is meant to last. You understand that code isn't "done" until it's tested and integrated into a CI/CD pipeline.
Problem-Solving Curiosity: You enjoy the "puzzle" of hardware/software interactions and don't mind getting your hands dirty in a complex codebase.
Bonus Skills (Nice to Have)
Container Exposure: You’ve used Docker, Kubernetes, or OpenShift and understand how they interact with the underlying OS.
DevOps Basics: You’ve worked with Jenkins, GitLab CI, or Ansible to automate your workflows.
Open Source Mindset: You’re comfortable navigating GitHub, reading other people’s code, and contributing to upstream projects (like the OPI Project).
The salary range for this position is $96,440.00 - $154,190.00. Actual offer will be based on your qualifications.
Pay Transparency
Red Hat determines compensation based on several factors including but not limited to job location, experience, applicable skills and training, external market value, and internal pay equity. Annual salary is one component of Red Hat’s compensation package. This position may also be eligible for bonus, commission, and/or equity. For positions with Remote-US locations, the actual salary range for the position may differ based on location but will be commensurate with job duties and relevant work experience.
About Red Hat
Red Hat is the world’s leading provider of enterprise open source software solutions, using a community-powered approach to deliver high-performing Linux, cloud, container, and Kubernetes technologies. Spread across 40+ countries, our associates work flexibly across work environments, from in-office, to office-flex, to fully remote, depending on the requirements of their role. Red Hatters are encouraged to bring their best ideas, no matter their title or tenure. We're a leader in open source because of our open and inclusive environment. We hire creative, passionate people ready to contribute their ideas, help solve complex problems, and make an impact.
Benefits
Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage
Flexible Spending Account - healthcare and dependent care
Health Savings Account - high deductible medical plan
Retirement 401(k) with employer match
Paid time off and holidays
Paid parental leave plans for all new parents
Leave benefits including disability, paid family medical leave, and paid military leave
Additional benefits including employee stock purchase plan, family planning reimbursement, tuition reimbursement, transportation expense account, employee assistance program, and more!
Note:
These benefits are only applicable to full time, permanent associates at Red Hat located in the United States.
Inclusion at Red Hat
Red Hat’s culture is built on the open source principles of transparency, collaboration, and inclusion, where the best ideas can come from anywhere and anyone. When this is realized, it empowers people from different backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences to come together to share ideas, challenge the status quo, and drive innovation. Our aspiration is that everyone experiences this culture with equal opportunity and access, and that all voices are not only heard but also celebrated. We hope you will join our celebration, and we welcome and encourage applicants from all the beautiful dimensions that compose our global village.

description_preview:
About Us
The Ammortal Chamber brings together multiple scientifically backed wellness technologies into one experience. The Chamber can be utilized by wellness clinics and inside the home. Our clients include specialty spas and clinics, sports teams, and individuals who are biohackers or athletes.
We are a small team with a startup culture. After our first year shipping a finished product on the market, we have shown strong growth. Our team is made up of hardware and software engineers, health professionals, and startup entrepreneurs.
As we continue expanding, this role offers hands-on experience, opportunities to grow into leadership, and the chance to make a tangible impact by developing and delivering cutting-edge wellness technology. You'll collaborate across disciplines to innovate and shape technologies that enhance well-being for our clients.
What is this role and why does it exist?
This role focuses on full-stack software development for our Chamber technology while supporting the existing product line. As a Software Engineer in this position, you'll work across the entire stack, frontend user interfaces to backend services and embedded systems, and building the software that powers our innovative wellness technology. You'll utilize modern technologies including Go, Python, microservice architecture, and MQTT; occasionally, you will contribute to first-gen Chamber maintenance and feature development.
This position is essential to Ammortal's mission. You'll be helping to build the future of our product while ensuring continuity with our current offerings. Our clients, speciality clinics serving patients to athletes optimizing their performance, depend on our Chambers daily. You'll work in a diverse, cross-functional environment where you'll tackle challenges spanning web applications, system-level programming, IoT communication, and containerized deployments. This role will also include some quality assurance and technical support responsibilities, giving you end-to-end ownership and deep understanding of our products. As we scale, your contributions will directly shape the architecture and capabilities that define the next generation of wellness technology.
Responsibilities:
Developing features and functionality for Chamber software across the full stack
Contributing to architectural decisions for our microservices-based platform
Maintaining and occasionally developing features for early-gen Chamber software
Participating in quality assurance processes to ensure software reliability and performance
Providing technical support for customer issues when needed
Collaborating with cross-functional teammates (software, hardware, operations, customer experience) to deliver robust end-to-end solutions
Skills To Excel
Attention to Detail: Strong attention to detail; organized and methodical in approach to both development and testing
Continuous Learning: Eagerness for hands-on learning of new technologies, languages, and architectural patterns
Diverse Environment Adaptability: Thrives working in diverse teams and technical environments, comfortable context-switching between different stacks and problem domains
Programming Versatility: Demonstrated ability to work with multiple programming languages and paradigms
System Thinking: Ability to understand and work across different layers of the stack, from UI to backend services to system-level code
Independent + Collaborative: Balances initiative and independence with knowing when to ask for help
Customer Focus: Understanding of how technical decisions impact user experience and customer success
Comfortable Multitasking: Comfortable managing multiple priorities and switching between tasks as needed
Process Adherence: Ability to take direction well and follow established development processes
Team Collaboration: Works effectively in a collaborative, cross-disciplinary team environment
Requirements
What technical knowledge do you need to perform in your role?
Required
Experience with at least one modern high-level programming language (JavaScript, Python, or similar)
Experience with at least one lower-level language (Go, C, C++, or similar)
Familiarity with Linux environments and command line usage
Experience with version control (Git)
Familiarity with a project management and tracking tool (e.g., Asana, Linear, Jira, etc)
Understanding of software development lifecycle and testing practices
Preferred
Experience with Next.js, React and Typescript for frontend development
Experience with Go for backend development
Familiarity with microservice architecture and design patterns
Experience with Docker and containerized deployments
Familiarity with Debian-based Linux systems
Experience with MQTT or other IoT communication protocols
Understanding of CI/CD pipelines (e.g. Github Actions workflows, etc.)
Familiarity with Shell scripting (Bash)
Familiarity with IoT, hardware, or hardware/software integration
Familiarity with AI-collaboration tools and agents
Qualifications - Nice To Haves
Previous experience in a full-stack development role, and/or
Previous experience working with embedded systems or IoT devices, and/or
Previous experience with real-time communication systems, and/or
Previous contributions to open-source projects or personal projects demonstrating breadth across the stack
Benefits
Pay range: $115,000 - $150,000
Benefits: 80% health, dental, vision covered
Location: Hybrid (office in Mars Hill, NC)
40-80% on-site, depending on your current assignments

Are you passionate about 3D graphics, GPUs, and pushing the boundaries of rendering technology? Have you ever dreamed of helping bring video games to life by creating tools that empower developers to integrate innovative new graphics techniques? Do you want to work with a fast, agile, and experienced team? Are you ready to move at the speed of light?
NVIDIA is seeking a deeply technical, creative and innovative software engineer help pioneer the next generation of Graphics Developer Tools. In this role, you will work closely with our research team to develop new tools and related technologies that not only streamline graphics performance but also support emerging technologies, like neural rendering, to enhance visual quality and efficiency.
What You'll Be Doing
As a key member of the team, you will create new technical designs and implement features while working in an agile environment. You can expect to:
Improve existing tools for NVIDIA GPUs, enabling developers to quickly identify and resolve rendering and performance issues.
Create innovative new tools that bridge AI & graphics in next generation workflows.
Collaborate closely with internal and external partners, including teams within NVIDIA such as the Compiler, Driver, Research, and GPU Architecture teams.
Drive technology discussions and provide feedback on system architecture.
Accurately estimate and prioritize tasks in order to create realistic delivery schedules.
Write fast, effective, maintainable, reliable and well-documented object-oriented code.
Document requirements and designs, and review documents with key partners.
Meet with the QA Department to develop test plans for new features.
What We Need To See
BS/MS in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or equivalent experience.
5+ years of relevant work experience in software development
Real passion for 3D graphics, AI, and low-level programming with 5+ years of relevant industry experience.
Excellent C/C++ programming skills.
Ability to provide accurate estimates to ensure delivery of software on time.
Knowledge of 3D Graphics Algorithms and GPU Architectures, with proficiency in at least one 3D Graphics API such as Direct3D, OpenGL, or Vulkan.
Demonstrated experience with AI and deep learning techniques, including familiarity with neural network architectures, CUDA, and frameworks such as TensorFlow or PyTorch.
Deep understanding of computer architecture concepts such as virtual memory, caches, registers, threads, and heterogeneous computing.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Ways To Stand Out From The Crowd
Familiarity with deep learning and AI, particularly in applying these technologies to enhance graphics performance and quality.
Background in the game industry, research, or in a field that requires high-performance graphics.
Be able to demonstrate initiative and determination to get things done.
NVIDIA is widely considered to be one of the technology world’s most desirable employers with some of the most forward-thinking and hardworking people in the world working here.

With our invention of the GPU - the engine of modern visual computing - the field has expanded to encompass video games, movie production, product design, medical diagnosis and scientific research. Today, we stand at the beginning of the next era, the AI computing era, ignited by a new computing model, GPU deep learning.

What this position is:
Full stack development across a range of products & domains - heavy focus on full stack web-based applications.
This role will be split between non-client work (building new features and continuing development & maintenance on our existing web-based products) and client work (including taking over some existing projects, as well as taking point on new projects).
NOTE: This role is NOT client facing. You will not be expected to manage client expectations or handle sales/contracts.
This role will work on a splattering of random tasks & projects, including product features, bug fixes, integrations, internal dashboards, workflow automation, data processing, and improvements to existing systems.
The types of projects we work on can vary, so we’re looking for someone who learns quickly, is comfortable working across different systems, and can adapt as priorities shift.
What we’re looking for:
These descriptions are always difficult to write because the subject is nuanced and software development is complex. Here’s my attempt to be concise: we’re looking for someone who
Is a capable developer even without AI
Is simultaneously comfortable leveraging AI to the hilt when it makes sense to do so
Can weigh & communicate the tradeoffs/risks of using AI more or less heavily on certain tasks/projects. Similarly, can communicate associated tech-debt and design risks
Can switch between “we need to do this quickly at the cost of [higher risk, lower quality, etc]” and “we need to do this diligently [possibly without AI]”
Makes an effort to understand the code they output, how it works, and what its shortcomings/risks are - even if the actual code was “written” by AI
(Sidenote: we
do
understand that if we decide to make heavy use of AI and move very quickly, then the level of understanding and familiarity with the code will be significantly less than if we spend the time to diligently design, write, and re-write it all by hand - those are all tradeoffs that we recognize, and simply need to be part of the discussion)
Familiar with Next, React, Prisma, PostgreSQL, and Typescript, or has transferable knowledge (Next, React, etc are all easy enough to pick up if you have a background in other programming languages/frameworks)
Hiring process:
Submit your resume. We’ll review it.
Intro Call: ~15 mins
Take-Home Assignment: ~2-3 hours; hard stop at half day
Second Call: 1 hour call with the agenda:
Discuss take-home & resume (~15-30 mins)
Time to discuss any questions you have (however much or little time you want/need)
Paid Trial: 1 day (~8 hours); $400;
If desired we can spread this out over 2-4 partial days to accommodate work or personal schedules
Final Thoughts & Process Notes:
It’s fairly common for us to get 1,000-2,000 responses to these job listings. We respond to everyone who applies, but due to the volume of applications we receive, if your application gets rejected during the resume screening process, then you’ll receive an automated batch email. You will work at the intersection of neural rendering, novel view synthesis, and generative modeling, training large-scale models on Matterport's proprietary data to solve problems that no existing dataset or model can address.
This is a hands-on research-and-engineering role for someone who wants to push the state of the art in 3D generative AI and ship it into a product used across 170+ countries. You will collaborate closely with fellow researchers, platform engineers, and product teams to translate frontier ideas into capabilities our customers can feel.
Responsibilities
Research, design, and train large-scale foundational models for 3D reconstruction and generative scene completion, leveraging Matterport's proprietary corpus of real-world spatial data.

Develop generative approaches — including diffusion models and video/3D generation — to complete occluded or missing regions, synthesize unobserved viewpoints, and enhance the realism and completeness of digital twins.
Design, implement, and optimize scalable training and inference pipelines for large 3D and multi-view datasets, including images, video, point clouds, and meshes.
